distribution.reason: Local emulator candidate. Observed closure flags (AGPL-3.0 emulator and SDK, GPL-3.0 vpcd handler, LGPL glib, GPL-2.0-or-later dual-license options in mbedTLS sources), actual-layer/generated-content review and digest-bound source-companion delivery remain incomplete; checker/consumer/proxy admission is separate.

constraints: Linux amd64/glibc, pico-hsm emulator only. Real SmartCard-HSM hardware, other readers, other backends, FIPS claims and other architectures/libcs are excluded. This qualifies OpenSC against pico-hsm, never real HSM hardware.

Both channels source-build unpatched OpenSC (release 0.27.1, rolling 0.27.1-339-g4f3ff51) with system OpenSSL 3.5.7 libcrypto.so.3; no legacy provider and no from-source OpenSSL. The pico-hsm backend pin (v6.6 plus pico-keys-sdk, mbedTLS v3.6.6, framework, mlkem and tinycbor) and the vsmartcard pin (virtualsmartcard-0.11) are shared across channels with one SDK build-freeze patch (frozen vendored mbedTLS, no configure-time self-update); upstream PKCS#11 semantics are unchanged.

Basic runtime has the module, libopensc, sc-hsm-tool, the pico-hsm emulator, the ifd-vpcd handler with its generated reader.conf entry, the stock opensc.conf, pcscd, base libraries and the exact extracted closure (6 whole packages, audited with ldd receipts). The openssl CLI, USB CCID drivers, the polkitd/dbus daemons, pkcs11-tool, opensc-tool, Python, checker, datasets and tracing are excluded; nothing links them.
The caller UID may be root or non-root with any primary group; both are qualified. No NSS wrapper or fixed group is required.

Bind writable /var/lib/p11lab; a private ephemeral /run/p11lab is required. /run/pcscd is an in-image symlink into the control tmpfs so the fixed daemon socket path works without a caller mount. Never share /run with another runtime. Each shard/client owns a separate volume, container, daemons and network namespace (the emulator and vpcd use the fixed loopback port 35963). Logs and pid state live under /run; the flash, lease and marker persist under /var/lib/p11lab/opensc-pico.

The emulator self-fabricates its 8 MiB flash in the owned state directory on first init; later operations resume it. First init initializes the fresh flash with the caller PINs over a pty and generates three on-card keys (P-256 id 01, RSA-2048 id 02, P-384 id 03); INITIALIZE is never re-run because it silently resets the token. Repeated init validates state and checks readiness like health, without consuming credentials.

Caller user PIN is 6..15 bytes single-line and caller SO-PIN is exactly 16 hexadecimal characters; both are required at first init only. No baked caller credentials or initialized flash ship. The token label stays the firmware default SmartCard-HSM; the post-initialize relabel path corrupts this emulator and is never used.

The token label is fixed natively as SmartCard-HSM at slot 0, token-present index 0; P11LAB_LABEL defaults to it and any other value is refused. SO login verifies shape eagerly (16 hex) and value only at SO-gated operations; the user PIN has a 3-try budget (two 0xa0 then 0xa4) and SO unblock via C_InitPIN restores it.

init/health/exec supervise pcscd plus the emulator for that operation only: subreaper adoption, volume/control leases, socket plus reader-with-card plus ATR-match plus native pre-login token readiness, daemon-death detection, signal forwarding, bounded logs and bounded terminate/kill/reap. exec retains both services for the complete application lifetime and preserves argv/status.

Provisioning uses only the pinned sc-hsm-tool INITIALIZE over a raw-mode pty with caller secrets on the pty (never argv/logs) plus in-process PKCS#11 keygen. The provision log carries only fixed prompt-answered lines. A card that cannot present the frozen ATR is refused before any PKCS#11 call.

Unknown/hidden entries, unsafe links/hardlinks/modes/sizes, changed non-secret configuration, stale daemon debris, missing flash and busy state are refused before native open. Failures retain partial state for investigation.

The general-token profile is retained after native on-card keygen plus P-256 independent verification and altered-message rejection in both generated and existing modes in both channels; wider mechanisms, multi-client concurrency, other readers/backends and provider-wide qualification are not asserted.

All runtime/consumer/checker/proxy artifacts remain blocked for distribution. Preserve exact provider sources, the 8-repository closure, Debian closure sources/notices and generated build inputs; source admission, public delivery and publication are separate gates.
